title: Resources in Kenya
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Start with the school compound: soil, water, trees, sunshine. Then widen to Kenya.

skills.key_step: The child names the natural resources of Kenya (land, soil, water, minerals, forests, wildlife, fish, sunshine, wind) and tells them from things people make.

floor.prerequisite: Names natural resources in the county.
floor.question: Name one natural resource in your county.
floor.answer: any of: soil, water, forest, minerals, wildlife

steps: Ask: did nature give it or did people make it?
If nature, it is a natural resource.

board.do: Write soil, a road, a forest, a building.

board.say: Is a road a natural resource?

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is a natural resource of Kenya?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what people used before they had money.

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is a natural resource?
misconceptions.repair: Sort cards into made by nature or made by people.

listen_for: No, resources are only things from nature
misconceptions.ask: Are skilled people a resource for Kenya?
misconceptions.repair: List what a nurse or a fundi gives the country.
Show the wind farm at Lake Turkana or a solar panel on a roof.

checks.question: Which is a natural resource: a forest or a bridge?
Give two natural resources found in Kenya.
checks.answer: any two of: land, soil, water, minerals, forests, wildlife, fish, sunshine, wind

skills.key_step: The child says prudent use means using resources carefully so they last and picks sustainable actions.
representations: action cards: lasts or runs out
a leaking tap and a bucket
contexts: fishing with the right net size
mending a leaking tap at school

board.do: Draw a forest with three trees cut down.

board.say: What should be done so the forest lasts?

misconceptions.ask: What does it mean to use a resource prudently?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a family that uses water carefully with one that wastes it.

listen_for: The forest grows back at once
misconceptions.ask: If people cut all the trees in a forest without planting new ones, what happens?
misconceptions.repair: Compare how long a tree takes to grow with how fast it can be cut.

misconceptions.ask: A family uses an empty jerrycan to store water. Is this reusing or recycling?
misconceptions.repair: Sort examples: a jar used again, plastic melted into a bucket.

misconceptions.ask: Can Kenya run short of water?
misconceptions.repair: Talk about a drought year and dry boreholes in the county.

checks.question: Give one way of using water prudently.
checks.answer: any of: mend leaks, close taps, harvest rainwater, reuse water

checks.question: Can forests run out if many trees are cut?
checks.answer: Yes, unless new trees are planted
